entities.name: PrismaSchemaOps
observations: 2026-06-09: Stack — Prisma v6.19.2 (ADR-0003), Postgres @ localhost:5432, db 'resumsify'. Migrations folder is prisma/migrations/, source of truth is prisma/schema.prisma.

2026-06-09: Baseline-drift capture migration shipped — 20260609180000_baseline_drift_capture. Consolidates ADR-0012 Asset tables + JobAsset.assetType→assetTypeId rename + ADR-0020 voiceDictationConsentedAt + DROP WorkLog_shiftId_idx. Live DB state unchanged; migration marked via `prisma migrate resolve --applied`. Fresh-clone `prisma migrate deploy` now reproduces live schema end-to-end (103/103 migrations).

2026-06-09: Convention going forward — NEVER use `prisma db execute` for column or table changes. Always author a real dated migration file via `prisma migrate dev --create-only`. The db-execute workaround was a one-time pragmatic crutch during drift; using it again will recreate the same problem.

2026-06-09: Intrinsic Prisma false-positive — `Unsupported("tsvector")?` columns cannot express the GENERATED expression in schema.prisma, so every `prisma migrate diff` will eternally report `ALTER COLUMN "search_vector" DROP DEFAULT`. NEVER include that line in a migration — Postgres rejects DROP DEFAULT on GENERATED columns (correct cleanup is DROP EXPRESSION, also inexpressible). This is permanent noise to ignore.

2026-06-09: Recovery recipe canonized at docs/workflows/recover-from-prisma-drift.md — shadow DB on same host → `migrate diff --from-migrations --to-schema-datamodel` → sanitize (skip tsvector line, reorder for FK safety, header comment with ADR refs) → author migration → `migrate resolve --applied` on live → validate fresh deploy on shadow → drop shadow.

2026-06-09: Windows PowerShell quirk — multi-line `run_in_terminal` blocks silently eaten. Workaround: single-line semicolon-joined commands. Also: `npx prisma db execute --stdin` never prints SELECT results, only 'Script executed successfully.' — use psql directly to inspect data.
2026-06-09: Reference commit 1f12fcc chore(prisma): baseline-drift capture migration (ADR-0012/0020).

2026-06-25: Prisma checked/unchecked variant runtime quirk (caught in ADR-0051 Sprint α' Commit 2, fix in f3b36df). When `prisma.<model>.create({ data })` is called with an EXPLICIT `id` field plus a scalar FK (e.g. `userId: 'foo'`), Prisma's runtime validator picks the CHECKED input variant (DocumentCreateInput), which has no scalar FK fields — only nested relation inputs like `user: UserCreateNestedOneWithoutDocumentsInput`. The validator then throws `Argument `user` is missing` even though the TS DocumentUncheckedCreateInput accepts the scalar form. TS compile-time + mocked unit tests cannot catch this — only live integration surfaces it (Schema-Faithful Mocks lesson generalizes: vi.fn() is shape-blind). FIX: use the relation `connect` form unconditionally when explicit id is present: `user: { connect: { id: input.userId } }`. The connect form is unambiguous in either variant. This pattern is now standard for all `createDocument`-like helpers in `src/lib/documents/`.

2026-06-25: Prisma client regen recovery loop on OneDrive-synced Windows (caught in ADR-0051 Sprint α' Commit 2). Symptom: `npx prisma generate` reports `EPERM: operation not permitted, rename query_engine-windows.dll.node.tmp32976 -> query_engine-windows.dll.node`. The `.tmp` rename collides with EITHER a running dev-server file handle on the query engine DLL OR OneDrive's file scanner. Generated TS .d.ts may regenerate successfully even when the runtime engine + cached `node_modules/.prisma/client/schema.prisma` snapshot DON'T — leading to a confusing state where TS shows `data?: string | null` but Prisma runtime rejects `data: null` because the cached schema.prisma still says `data String` (required). FIX: (1) kill all dev-server node processes (`Stop-Process -Id <pid>`); (2) `npx prisma generate` — if EPERM, `Start-Sleep -Seconds 2; npx prisma generate` (OneDrive usually releases within 1-2s); (3) restart dev server. Verify the regen took by grepping `node_modules/.prisma/client/schema.prisma` for the changed field — if the TS d.ts disagrees with the cached schema.prisma, the engine is stale and runtime will still reject. Add the cached schema.prisma check to the diagnostic toolkit.
